solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Restaurant rubbish is strewn initially beside lake (10)

indicatorNotes.beside: puts the pieces next to each other

blocks.note: Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

annotation.surface: Litter lies scattered beside a lakeside restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in spit-roasted meat. 'Strewn' looks like an anagram signal but only lends its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant that serves meat roasted on a spit.

entries.clue: Sanction process of becoming a rodent? (12)

blocks.note: the jokey sense: split the word into a rodent plus the suffix meaning 'the process of making into'

annotation.surface: A whimsical question about some creature turning into a rodent.
annotation.walkthrough: The suffix -ification means 'the process of making into', so the word can be read jokily as becoming a rat; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Ratification is formal approval, a sanction given to a treaty or decision.

entries.clue: Somewhere along rocky height you and I stand high (5)

indicatorNotes.Somewhere along: places WE at a point partway along TOR, i.e. inside it

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop
you and I together are we

annotation.surface: Two walkers pause somewhere on a rocky summit, standing high.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere along' is an unusual way to say one thing sits inside another. A tor is a rocky outcrop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
annotation.definitionFit: To tower is to stand high above one's surroundings.

entries.clue: Agent grasses up enemy in the end (3)

indicatorNotes.in the end: take each word's end, its last letter

blocks.note: last letters of grasseS, uP, enemY

annotation.surface: An informer betrays the enemy in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grasses up' is British slang for informs on, which suits an agent so well that it hides that its letters are the fodder. 'In the end' seems to go only with 'enemy' but applies to all three words.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a secret agent gathering intelligence is a spy, the sense the informer surface leans on.

entries.clue: Quickness of European Pole on board? (6)

blocks.note: a sprit is a spar on a sailing boat

annotation.surface: Asks how quick a European, a Polish person, is aboard a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is capitalised to suggest a Polish person; it is a pole on board a boat, a sprit. The question mark flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Esprit is liveliness of mind, quickness of wit.

entries.clue: I will turn up. I visit mostly without reason (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, reading upward reverses GO
indicatorNotes.mostly: drops the last letter of CALL

blocks.note: CALL, a visit, less its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone promising to show up, but only visiting mostly without any reason.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like arrive; it splits into 'turn', a go, and 'up', which reverses it in a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Illogical means lacking reason or sound thinking.

entries.clue: Electrical unit checked after removal of terminals (6)

indicatorNotes.after removal of terminals: terminals are the end letters, here removed

annotation.surface: An electrician's unit stopped working once its terminals were taken off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terminals' suits the electrical surface but means the first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: current is measured in amps, named after the physicist André-Marie Ampère.

entries.clue: Style of swimming starkers to be changed (12)

indicatorNotes.changed: the letters are altered in order

annotation.surface: Swimming naked, with someone about to change their stroke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starkers' is British slang for naked. 'To be' looks like part of the instruction but is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Breaststroke is a swimming stroke done face down with frog-like kicks.

entries.clue: Nearly tan … half browny? (5)

indicatorNotes.Nearly: drops the last letter of TAN
indicatorNotes.half: keeps just the back half of BROWNY

blocks.note: last three of BROWNY's six letters

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: tawny is a colour close to tan and somewhat brownish.
annotation.definitionFit: Tawny is an orangey-brown colour, near tan and half way to brown.

entries.clue: Perhaps vinyl LP more damaged around the start of Yesterday (7)

indicatorNotes.damaged: the letters of LP MORE are rearranged

annotation.surface: A vinyl record of the Beatles' Yesterday gets more damaged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vinyl' and 'LP' suggest records, but vinyl is here the plastic, an example of a polymer; 'Perhaps' marks the example.
annotation.definitionFit: Vinyl (PVC) is a polymer, so 'perhaps vinyl' points to it.

entries.clue: High region covered in thick mist earlier (9)

indicatorNotes.High: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.covered in: the scrambled letters sit inside FOG

annotation.surface: An upland area was shrouded in fog earlier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High region' reads as upland, but 'High' is the anagram signal, in its drugged sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Foregoing means preceding, said or happening earlier.

entries.clue: Donkey left in large area of pasture (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the donkey and left go inside GRAND

annotation.surface: A donkey turned out into a big field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large area' looks like one phrase, but 'large' belongs to the wordplay and 'area of pasture' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Grassland is land covered in grass, used for pasture.

entries.clue: Time regularly needed for retrial (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take letters at even spacing

annotation.surface: Time is routinely needed to prepare a retrial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time regularly needed' reads as a statement about court schedules; 'regularly' actually works on 'retrial'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an era is a period of time, as in the Victorian era.

entries.clue: See heads on Camra’s own choice of alcoholic drink (5)

indicatorNotes.See heads on: tells you to look at the head, the first letter, of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Camra's, own, choice, of, alcoholic

annotation.surface: The real-ale campaign's pick of alcoholic drink.
annotation.walkthrough: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British beer group, so the surface points at booze; the answer is famously non-alcoholic.
annotation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from cocoa powder and milk.

entries.clue: Make wooden box with key inserted (6)

indicatorNotes.with: joins the box to what goes in it

blocks.note: a crate is a wooden box

annotation.surface: Instructions for building a wooden box with a key fitted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a lock but is a musical key, one of A to G.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both verbs mean to bring something into being.

entries.clue: Top clubs recharge one’s batteries (5)

annotation.surface: Top football clubs take a break to recharge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top clubs' reads as elite teams, but 'Top' is the definition and 'clubs' just gives C.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the highest point of a hill or wave is its crest.

entries.clue: Gateway drink — a lager at first (6)

annotation.surface: Port and then a lager: a gateway drink to heavier drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gateway drink' reads as a phrase about a first step, but 'Gateway' is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name an entrance, portal being the grander word, also used for a website that leads elsewhere.

entries.clue: English appeal over draw (3)

indicatorNotes.over: turns E + IT over, reversing it

annotation.surface: An English appeal is made about a drawn match.
annotation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is an old convention from the 1920s 'It girl'.
annotation.definitionFit: A tie is a draw, a game with equal scores.

entries.clue: What could be on actor is easy to carry around on location (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, one thing on another sits next to it, so LIGHT comes placed on, i.e. after, SPOT

blocks.note: light things are easy to carry

annotation.surface: An actor lugging something portable to a location shoot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal but belongs to 'easy to carry around', meaning light.
annotation.definitionFit: A spotlight is the beam trained on an actor on stage.

entries.clue: Character of flowing magma (5)

indicatorNotes.flowing: the letters of MAGMA move about

annotation.surface: Describes the nature of molten rock pouring from a volcano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests nature or personality; it is a letter, here the Greek one.
annotation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter, or character, of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: One rejected from openly gay actors (7)

blocks.note: the cast is a play's actors

annotation.surface: Someone shunned by a troupe of openly gay actors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One rejected from' reads as a single phrase; 'from' only links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a person cast out by their group, which the surface's rejection from a troupe mirrors.

entries.clue: Come running about a brief character role (5)

indicatorNotes.running: sets the letters of COME in motion
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go around A

annotation.surface: An actor hurries over for a small part.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come running' reads as a phrase meaning hurry, but 'running' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small but distinctive role for a well-known actor.

entries.clue: Prompt remedy banishing runs (3)

indicatorNotes.banishing: to banish is to expel, so the letter for runs is driven out of the remedy

annotation.surface: A quick treatment that ends a bout of the runs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The runs' is slang for diarrhoea, which the surface plays on; in cricket notation R is runs.
annotation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt, such as an actor's signal to speak.

entries.clue: Contaminate fully-fledged Ecstasy with speed (10)

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

annotation.surface: Cutting pure ecstasy with the drug speed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like the amphetamine in this drugs scene, but it means rate.
annotation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to contaminate by adding inferior substances.
